text:
maya: bringing up a quantized reranker (distil-bert-rank q4) for production. i want to validate quality and per-query stability vs fp16 before we flip traffic. primary metrics: NDCG@5, NDCG@10, MRR@10. dataset suggestions and any formatting caveats?
jon: +1 to run on the recent prod-sample (week-of-2026-03-01) and ms-marco dev for comparability. also run on our session-holdout split so we catch user-specific distribution shifts.
ravi: for docs we should compare two formatting schemes: 1) title-first ("TITLE: {title}\nBODY: {body}") and 2) concat-with-markers ("[T]{title}[D]{body}"). hard negatives matter a lot for rerankers — use top-100 BM25 as soft negatives and our human-labeled pool as hard negs.
alex: metrics + stability: compute NDCG@5/@10 and MRR@10, then bootstrap per-query CIs (1000 resamples) and report fraction of queries with non-overlapping CIs between fp16 and q4. also compute effect size (mean delta / stdev).
alex: eval command i'll run (example):
```
python eval/rerank_eval.py \
  --model=distil-bert-rank-q4 \
  --baseline=distil-bert-rank-fp16 \
  --queries=prod_sample_2026-03-01.tsv \
  --qfmts=title_first,concat_tags \
  --metrics=ndcg@5,ndcg@10,mrr@10 \
  --bootstrap=1000 \
  --save-artifact s3://redwood-evals/rerank/q4-stability-run.tar.gz
```
daphne: watch out: quantization can compress logit dynamic range causing score compression — leads to systematic downranking of fringe positives. please also run a small calibration on a dev fold: temperature scaling or a simple linear regressor on logits -> rank scores. i can share a tiny script.
daphne: quick calibration call: `python eval/calibrate.py --preds raw_logits.npy --labels labels.npy --outscale scale.npy` — then apply `score = logits * scale` before computing NDCG.
eval-bot: automated snapshot: run-id=q4-stab-20260305-01 | datasets=msmarco-dev,prod_sample | ndcg@10: fp16=0.432, q4=0.426, delta=-0.006 (p=0.032) | mrr@10: fp16=0.281, q4=0.277 | per-query non-overlap=22% | notes=small but significant drop on tail queries with long docs. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/rerank/q4-stability-run.tar.gz
maya: thanks. can we also test a pairwise-loss trained reranker vs our pointwise baseline? sometimes quantization affects the margin distribution differently. if pairwise holds better under q4, that's useful.
jon: i'll queue the pairwise run and the formatting ablation. will also log raw logits + ranks (`--save-raw`) so we can diff distributions. queue ETA ~ 3 hrs. link to run logs when ready -> https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-evals/rerank/q4-stability-run.tar.gz
ravi: small request: include per-query example bucket breakdowns (short queries, navigational, long tail) in the report. those categories show the biggest metric shifts historically.
alex: ack. i'll add a small notebook to compute per-segment bootstrap CIs and a chart of percentile delta.
maya: perfect — please ping when artifacts land. if q4 drop is concentrated on <5% of queries we can consider selective fallback (fp16 for critical routes). :thumbsup:
jon: noted — will follow up in thread with run timestamps and brief summary.
